newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW-Few IPOs due in holiday slowdow.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW-Few IPOs due in holiday slowdow.

text.p: Few initial public offerings are slated this week as Wall Street underwriters and investors ready for the Christmas and New Year holidays.
"Darkness is settling over the land. It happens every year. I don't expect anything to come public in the next two weeks," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket.

Only two small IPOs are due next week, both from National Securities -- Multimedia Access Corp, which develops video communications products for personal computers and workstations and Vita Food Products, a Chicago maker of specialty food products.
"For the next two weeks, The Street's not really even pushing any deals. 1996 is pretty much a wrap at this point," said Matt Considine, portfolio manager of the Phoenix Mid Cap Fund.

"Last week was pretty decent, but this week I'm not expecting much at all. It's early, but I'm hearing demand in the next quarter is looking really horrible," said Vince Slavin, who tracks IPOs for Cantor Fitzgerald.

Last week, several companies made solid market debuts including payment processor BA Merchant Services and Delia's Inc., which sells clothes for young women through catalogs. But a few fell below their issue prices.
"Both Larscom Inc. and Swisher International Group Inc checked into the heartbreak hotel," Fitzgibbon said.
Larscom stock closed at $11.375 Friday on Nasdaq, below its IPO price of $12 a share. Swisher stock, on the New York Stock Exchange, closed at $16, below its IPO price of $17 a share.
